stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$. Write $|X|$ for its underlying topological space, obtained from the equivalence classes of morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ from spectra of fields. The fibre product of algebraic spaces is understood in the category of algebraic spaces. For an étale presentation $U\to X$ by a scheme, $R=U\times_XU$ is its groupoid of arrows with projections $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$. A morphism is representable if every base change along a map from a scheme has scheme source.

For $x\in|X|$, condition $(\alpha)_x$ means every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has only finitely many points over $x$. Condition $(\beta)_x$ means there is a monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$. Condition $(\gamma)_x$ means there is a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ representing $x$, equivalently for every affine étale $U\to X$ both fibres over $x$ of $|U|\to|X|$ and $|U\times_XU|\to|X|$ are finite. The conditions $(\alpha),(\beta),(\gamma)$ mean the corresponding pointwise property holds at every $x$.

An algebraic space $X$ is decent if every point $x\in|X|$ admits a quasi-compact representing monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$. It is reasonable if every affine étale morphism $U\to X$ has universally bounded finite fibres, and very reasonable if it is Zariski-locally covered by quasi-compact surjective étale schemes. A morphism $f:X\to Y$ is *decent* (respectively reasonable, very reasonable or with property $(\beta)$) if $X\times_YT$ has that property for every scheme $T\to Y$. Property $(\beta)$ for a space means that every point can be represented by a monomorphism from a field spectrum.

For a cartesian square of algebraic spaces $W=X\times_YZ$, with projections $p:W\to X$ and $q:W\to Z$, let $x\in|X|$ and $z\in|Z|$ have common image $y\in|Y|$. Define $F_{x,z}=\{w\in|W|:p(w)=x,\ q(w)=z\}$. For a field representative $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)\to Y$, the fibre $X_y=X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)$ carries its ordinary Zariski topology, and the set $F_{x,z}$ is the fibre of the corresponding map of point spaces.

Let $X$ be an algebraic space locally of finite type over a field $k$.
Consider the conditions
\begin{enumerate}
\item $|X|$ is a finite set,
\item $|X|$ is a discrete space,
\item $\dim(|X|) = 0$,
\item $\dim(X) = 0$,
\item $X \to \operatorname{Spec}(k)$ is locally quasi-finite,
\end{enumerate}
Then (2), (3), (4), and (5) are equivalent.
If $X$ is decent, then (1) implies the others.
